goal.source_text: Cut fin drag as much as you can while keeping the stability margin at least 1.5 calibers and the flutter margin at least 1.5. You can change the root chord, semi-span, sweep and taper; keep the thickness.
assumptions: Darwin may change root_chord, taper_ratio, semi_span, sweep_deg; it holds thickness, edge_profile, fin_count fixed.
Thickness is kept at its current value.
Drag is measured as total fin-set drag (drag_n) at the existing design velocity of 120 m/s.

payload.rationale: Flutter margin is the binding constraint with only 0.1007 slack. Reducing root chord may lower fin stiffness but also area; increasing taper ratio below 0.5 might reduce tip mass and raise flutter velocity. Bracketing opposite shifts tests tradeoff.

payload.explanation: Reducing root chord and taper ratio decreased fin area 25%, cutting drag slightly (-0.675%) but lowering flutter velocity 3.20% and stability margin 3.13%. The flutter got worse, not better; less area reduced both stiffness and inertia, but stiffness loss dominated. Drag nearly unchanged because profile drag is small.
payload.lesson: Flutter velocity is sensitive to chord reduction; smaller area may hurt flutter margin more than drag.

payload.explanation: Root chord cut from 75 to 60 mm and sweep increased to 35 deg. Drag barely changed (down only 0.558%), not the predicted 5-15% drop, because profile drag reduction was offset by increased induced drag from lower aspect ratio. Stability margin unexpectedly fell by 7.06% to 1.62 cal, still safe. Flutter margin improved 6.26% to 1.875, likely due to higher sweep and reduced fin area (down 20%).
payload.lesson: Sweep changes trade stability for flutter margin, not just drag.

payload.explanation: Reducing root chord by 10 mm cut planform area 16.7% and fin mass 16.7%, raising flutter margin 5.56%. Drag barely changed (-0.383%), much less than predicted (-5% to -16%). Stability margin fell 11.6% to 1.433, violating the 1.5 limit, so solver rejected the design.
payload.lesson: Shortening root chord reduces stability margin without meaningful drag savings on this fin set.

payload.explanation: Taper ratio reduced from 0.35 to 0.25 while semi_span unchanged. Drag fell 0.496%, far less than predicted (-12% to -4%), likely because planform area decreased 7.41% but induced drag component barely changed. Stability margin decreased 4.85%, within predicted direction but slightly less than lower bound. Flutter margin dropped 5.32%, matching prediction.
payload.lesson: Taper reduction beyond current design yields minimal drag benefit and slightly worsens stability and flutter margins.
